previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with altered mental status, fever, and hyperkalemia after missing a dialysis session. He had a history of dialysis line infections and seizure disorder. Initial workup revealed a potassium of 6.8, treated with insulin, glucose, and kayexalate, followed by hemodialysis. Blood cultures grew beta strep group C and coagulase-negative staph, prompting IV vancomycin for suspected line-related bacteremia. A CT head showed no acute findings. The patient refused a lumbar puncture. His mental status improved, and he remained stable after dialysis. Despite recommendations to complete IV antibiotics inpatient, he chose to leave against medical advice on hospital day two. Arrangements were made for IV antibiotics during outpatient dialysis. He was counseled on medication adherence, particularly for seizure prevention.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo m with h/o ESRD on HD, sCHF (EF 40%), and seizure disorder 
presents from HD after having two witnessed seizures.
.
# Seizure: Patient has known history of seizure disorder.  
Seizures most commonly occur in the setting of hemodialysis. 
Patient states he was instructed this week to start taking his 
antiepilectics prior to HD instead of waiting until afterwards.  
Unfortunately, patient reports he was running late this morning 
on his way to HD and missed his morning dose.  Per his medical 
records, patient's seizure activity is most commonly associated 
with poor adherence to his regimen. Patient confirms that it is 
not a failure in his regimen, but just that he simply did not 
take his medications. He has no evidence of underlying 
infection, trauma, intoxication, or sleep deprivation to 
instigate seizures.  Patient was continued on previous home 
regimen:
.
Keppra Regimen:  500 mg tablets; one tablet prior to morning 
dialysis, one tablet after morning dialysis and one tablet in 
the evening (total of 3 pills a day).  On days that he does not 
have dialysis he should take one tablet in the morning and one 
tablet in the evening (total of 2 pills a day). 
.
Trileptal Regimen: On days that you do not have dialysis please 
take one tablet in the morning and one tablet in the evening 
(total of two tablets).  On days that you have dialysis please 
take one tablet before dialysis, one tablet after dialysis, and 
one tablet in the evening (total of three pills).
.
Access to medications was a challenge on this admission.  
Patient had recently had his medications filled on ___.  He 
misplaced all of his medications on the day of his admission. He 
was not able to have his medications refilled prior to discharge 
because he just had them filled two weeks prior, he had no 
money, and his pharmacy is not open on the weekends. 
Complicating the situation the ___ Orange Line called the 
pharmacy to alert them that the patient's medications were found 
and that they were being held in their office.  However, when we 
returned the call to the ___ they denied any knowledge of 
finding his medications. Patient was discharged on ___ 
___ with a 24 hour supply of antiepilectic medications.  He 
is to go to his pharmacy on ___ to attempt to have new 
prescriptions filled.  
.
# ?LLL Pneumonia: Concern for LLL pneumonia was based on 
preliminary chest x-ray read in the Emergency Department. 
Patient is at increased risk of pneumonia given susceptiblity to 
aspiration during seizure activity.  It is unlikely that he 
would already have a pneumonia after this mornings seizure 
activity.  Patient reports being npo before his seizure.  Final 
read of chest x-ray did not suggests a new pulmonary process. 
Patient denies any respiratory symptoms, fevers, or chills. He 
was afebrile on exam with no evidence of consolidation. WBC 
count was wnl. Patient was given no further antibiotics after 
admission to the medicine floor.
.
# Chronic kidney disease: ESRD on HD.  Patient underwent HD four 
times this week to treat his volume overload.  The morning of 
admission patient denies the sensation of volume overload.  He 
underwent the first 1.5 hours of HD before he began to seize and 
HD was terminated. Patient with no need for emergent dialysis on 
arrival to ED. Patient underwent HD the following day on 
___.   Plan to continue previous HD schedule.  
.
# Recent Bacteremia:  On prior admission patient found to have 
one out of four bottles positive for Strep group C.  Likely 
represents a contaminant.  However, because patient presented on 
that admission with fever and altered mental status he was 
treated with vancomycin per HD protocol. Source of bacteremia 
(?) unknown, presumed line infection.  Line was not changed on 
prior admission.  No evidence on exam of line infection today. 
Patient remains afebrile with normal WBC count. Vancomycin level 
is therapeutic on this admission. Patient is to complete 
vancomycin course with vancomycin per HD as outlined on prior 
discharge.

# Non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: Stable. Continue home digoxin and 
aspirin.
